To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

referencing change in a target stimulus sparks curiosity and information seeking and that these effects can have positive or negative implications for people’s evaluations depending on whether they are motivated to seek favorable or unfavorable information about that stimulus.

(1) referencing change decreases longevity perceptions; (2) this change-induced curiosity motivates people, but only when they can seek information about the change, to search for more information; (3) this information search can lead to favorable or unfavorable evaluations, depending on whether the information found is positive or negative; and (4) when information is not available, referencing change has a negative impact on evaluations.

Change references decrease perceptions of longevity, but also spark curiosity about the target object or entity, a desire to learn more, which can enhance people’s evaluations of it when they find favorable information, and depress their evaluations when they find unfavorable information.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
referencing a change in a target stimulus sparks curiosity, which motivates information search.
change references spark information seeking, which enhances or depresses people’s evaluations, depending on the nature of the further information.
change appeals are effective in promoting persuasion, and this effect is mediated by the curiosity and information search processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
referencing that something changed can have a positive effect on attitudes toward the changed object or entity when the information environment is conducive to information seeking.

change references are a double-edged sword: they can increase curiosity and information seeking about an object or entity, but this effect can be positive or negative depending on the availability of information.
change is an important aspect of human cognition and that it can affect our attitudes and behaviors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
referencing change can spark curiosity, which can lead to positive or negative evaluations, depending on the context.

change references are a powerful and ubiquitous tool in the persuasive arsenal of advertisers, politicians, and other communicators, but that their persuasive power depends on whether the change is favorable or unfavorable, and on whether further information is available.
